authorized: decision 1 on PR #101: a re-drawn second run including the two admitted forks with a mined positive
hypothesis: When the collector's nominator fires falsely, the consumer's turn changes less, and its reasoning acknowledges the nomination without acting on it more often, under advisory framing than imperative; and the difference falls as the nominator's precision rises.
fork: a main-lane turn.request of an archived capture drive at a register turn, re-fired verbatim with its recorded sampler parameters; the nomination appended to the last user message
headroom: the (b) headroom pilot's admitted set (headroom.json of the (b) record, consumed by digest) if the box is still instance 2026-09-20 at the window's start (fingerprint check and canary); otherwise the pilot is re-run on the new instance under the same rule (two no-nomination draws agree on (tool, target) and emit a command) and the new instance registered before any fork fires
sample: the two admitted forks carrying a mined positive (drive-08#t9s24, drive-09#t2s8) are in the sample by construction; 98 more are drawn once by seed 393 from the other admitted forks; the same 100 forks at every rung
true_nominations: mined positives only, as in (b): one per mined-positive fork; at rung p each of the two draws a true nomination with probability p, so the realisable true share is at most 0.02 on any rung; the true-nomination control fork is drive-08#t9s24 with its mined positive, fired before the run as the refusal gate and again in the run as an ordinary sample fork
ladder_reading: nominal: no rung claim is adjudicable from this register, stated before the run; the six rungs are six seeded assignments of a false nomination per fork over the same 100 forks and the rule's 'every rung' reads over them as replicate stability; the per-session cost = false-nomination change rate x (1 - p) is reported as the precision arm; the realised true share per rung is reported beside the nominal rung
nomination_lines: byte-identical to (b): imperative and advisory as posted on #89 2026-09-20 (5747608246); the same entry under all three framings of a fork within a rung
sham: a passage of exactly the advisory line's character length from the prose of a register turn of a different drive; source row recorded
turn_change: tool = first word of the extracted command after comment stripping (exercise extract-command, the drive loop's extractor; a leading '#' comment is not a tool); target = first path-like argument else the second word; a response with no command against one with a command is changed; OR the reply's prose before the command states a correction to, supersession of, replacement of or removal of the entry the nomination named (the edit field of the blind judge); the raw-extractor (tool, target) grade and the comment-stripped (tool, target) grade alone are reported beside, never adjudicating
record_edit: the ratified endpoint's third arm, unmeasured in (b) (decision 6): a two-way field 'edit' in {yes, no} by the blind judge over the reply's prose before the command, not the reasoning; yes iff the prose states the named entry is superseded, no longer holds, is wrong, should be updated or removed, or supplies replacement text for it; merely mentioning, questioning, checking, or affirming the entry is no
acknowledgement: names: any anchor of the nominated entry (the gym's literal::anchors) or the phrase 'working record' in the reasoning (thinking-on forks) or the prose before the command; if named, a three-way grade accepts / questions / declines by the blind judge's verdict field, over reasoning and prose; reported beside the verdict, never folded in
judge: one fresh Claude Code subagent per batch on Sonnet (model: sonnet at launch), the model read off each subagent's transcript and declared per batch in judge/judge.json; reads only judge/prompt.md (version 2, digest posted before the first fork) and its batch file; every non-control arm row is judged (imperative, advisory, sham; 1,800 rows in 50 batches of 36 plus 4 keyed controls each); items carry an opaque id, the register's entry text, the reasoning (thinking-on forks) and the prose before the command, and NOT the appended line, so the judge is blind to the arm as well as to the key; the key is withheld; each batch scored by judge-score: exit 0 keyed, 1 any control miss on either field (batch void), 2 malformed
void_protocol: a void batch (judge-score exit 1: a control miss on either field) is re-judged by a fresh instance under the same prompt, batch file and key; a malformed output (exit 2: ids missing, extra or out of order, or a field outside its vocabulary) is not a verdict and is likewise re-judged by a fresh instance, kept under judge/malformed-NN[b].json; up to three instances per batch, void and malformed outputs both counting; the void verdicts are kept under judge/void-NN[b].json, read by nothing; a batch unjudged after three instances has its rows carry edit = null and verdict = null, and a fork-rung with a null edit on either framing is excluded from that rung's changed rate pairwise, the count reported
judge_controls: keyed controls authored before the first batch, drawn from the (b) record's committed replies and keyed by hand for both fields, at least twelve, with at least four keyed edit = yes; judge/controls.json digest posted on #89 before the first fork
grading_orders: every deterministic grade (extract, tool_target, changed, names) is taken over the raw rows and over the committed rows after the home-prefix collapse; the committed grades are over the committed rows; the two gradings are diffed row by row and any difference declares grading order a regime factor in regimen.toml with the rows listed (decision 7)
primary: the rate of changed turns (turn_change above) on false nominations, advisory against imperative, at each rung, paired by fork
secondary: the acknowledgement grade and the (tool, target)-only change rates, reported beside the verdict
controls: the true-nomination control fork: a mined positive whose turn is the voiding step must read changed under both framings, or the run refuses

shuffled-framing null, pre-registered: arm labels permuted within fork, 9,999 permutations seeded, on every computable rung the null's mean advisory-minus-imperative difference within 0.02 of zero, or the result is inconclusive whatever the rule says (decision 5)
the sham arm as the perturbation floor
every grader's demonstrated failure in the instrument's selftest, the judge scorer's control-miss and malformed refusals included
substrate: the box instance at the window's start, expected 2026-09-20 (registered), pinned engine, production model and flags, each fork's own sampler parameters; verify-box before and after; production config untouched
box_time: 2,400 rows at the (b) mean of 5.6 s a row is about 3.7 h plus the control fork; about 4 h in the announced window, 5.2 h if the headroom pilot must be re-run on a new instance
readings_posted: every reading under decision-rule.toml [readings] is posted on #89 before the first fork; a reading not posted there is not applied
pilot: before ratification the judge prompt and controls were piloted on one batch of the (b) record's rows on Sonnet: the first pilot voided on an ambiguous control (replaced, the edit definition tightened), the second returned 38 objects for 40 items (malformed; the prompt now asks for the count and malformed outputs are covered above); pilot verdicts are read by nothing and no pilot touched the box
